question: Should OpenClaw accept a default-on user isolation contract for memory-core now, and what exact `memory.isolation` config semantics must be guaranteed before this PR continues?
rationale: This changes durable memory privacy boundaries and public config defaults; automation can identify defects but cannot choose the product/security contract for existing multi-user deployments.

options.title: Continue after repair and proof
options.body: Keep this PR as a candidate only after the default-on bug, option plumbing, merge conflicts, and two-user builtin/QMD proof are resolved.

options.title: Replace with canonical design work
options.body: Pause this PR and sponsor a narrower maintainer-reviewed implementation from the open multi-user isolation issue.

options.title: Defer default-on isolation
options.body: Require an explicit opt-in isolation mode first, preserving shared-memory behavior until the migration and security model are settled.

recommendation.title: Continue after repair and proof
recommendation.body: Keep this PR as a candidate only after the default-on bug, option plumbing, merge conflicts, and two-user builtin/QMD proof are resolved.
